comparator.name: Business Analytics
comparator.sourceNotes: UvA requires 60 EC in each year. Mathematics, programming and statistics prepare students for machine learning, econometrics and operations research. The final year includes a 30 EC elective semester, three required courses and two parallel 6 EC thesis courses.
components: AI, Privacy and Global Cybersecurity for Business Analytics

core: Mathematics, computing and business analysis integrated to improve organizational decisions
Calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics and mathematical optimization for business models
Programming, data management, machine learning and AI for organizational data
Business economics, finance and organizational applications of analytics
adjacent: Advanced algorithms, computing and mathematical methods for optimization
Prediction, customer analytics and business strategy informed by data
Responsible decisions with business data and artificial intelligence
questions: How can organizations use data and models to improve resource allocation and decisions?
How can prediction, customer information and market data shape business decisions?
How should organizations use AI and data responsibly?

alternatives.label: Business analytics across mathematics, data and organisations
alternatives.concept: Builds from mathematics, programming and business foundations to machine learning, algorithms, econometrics and market research. The quantitative courses support work on business decisions and consumer behaviour, while UvA has a longer operations research sequence and dedicated analytics projects.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has substantial quantitative, computational and business study; no one strand alone defines it.
progression: Mathematics, programming and research methods precede advanced work. The selected courses fit the six planned semesters and their formal prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Algorithms, AI and mathematical optimisation
alternatives.concept: Studies how to design algorithms, search for good solutions and make decisions under uncertainty. Advanced algorithms, numerical methods, reinforcement learning and software development give this option its technical focus. Business and econometrics provide applications, while UvA goes further into specialist business analytics.
alternatives.labelReason: Advanced computing, mathematics and AI occupy the curricular differences from the integrated route.
alternatives.distinctness: Software development, linear systems, advanced calculus and reinforcement learning replace marketing, market research, AI in business and deep learning in the closest option.
progression: Mathematics, programming and research methods precede advanced work. The selected courses fit the six planned semesters and their formal prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Data-informed markets, finance and strategy
alternatives.concept: Uses statistics, machine learning and econometrics alongside consumer behaviour, market research and finance. Digital strategy and international business add context for decisions about products and markets. UvA goes further into formal marketing models and operations research.
alternatives.labelReason: The course set has a substantive business and market sequence supported by data and quantitative methods.
alternatives.distinctness: Microeconomics, digital strategy, international business and banking replace numerical methods, advanced algorithms, AI decision-making and AI optimisation in the closest option.
progression: Mathematics, programming and research methods precede advanced work. The selected courses fit the six planned semesters and their formal prerequisites.

candidates.label: Predictive business modelling for markets and finance

selection.assessment: The first option balances business, mathematics and computing. The second puts more weight on algorithms and mathematical models. The third applies analytics to markets, finance and strategy. The three options differ by at least four courses in each direction. Responsible AI is a further interest and appears within the first and third options through study of AI governance.

blocks: Both study the pricing of financial assets and the role of risk. UCR also examines banking and monetary policy.
Both examine responsible uses of AI in organisations. UvA also studies data privacy and cybersecurity directly.
UvA develops consulting skills for analytics work in organisations.
Both use regression and statistical inference to estimate economic relationships and make predictions.
Both examine questions about people at work. UCR studies organisational behaviour, while UvA uses HR data to answer those questions.
Both use financial statements and accounting information to assess performance.
Both study venture opportunities, customer needs and business models. UvA applies them in a hackathon.
UvA offers a minor, an exchange, electives or an internship combined with electives. The UvA Business Analytics internship carries 12 EC and requires 90 EC already completed.
Both study customer evidence to inform marketing. UvA specifically teaches purchase prediction, choice and marketing-mix models.
UvA requires this 6 EC project alongside the 6 EC Skills course. UCR’s optional research element sits outside the illustrated schedules.
This 6 EC course develops design research and thesis writing alongside the Research Project.
Both develop differentiation and integration for mathematical modelling.
Both cover matrices, linear systems, vector spaces and eigenvalues.
Both develop probability distributions and statistical inference. UvA teaches these topics across two courses.
UvA requires a second linear algebra course. UCR covers some related topics in Linear Algebra, including eigenvalues and orthogonality.
Both teach linear and discrete optimisation. UvA develops operations research models, while UCR also studies search in AI.
UvA devotes a course to modelling uncertain operations. UCR teaches probabilistic decisions in AI, but has no equivalent operations research sequence in these options.
UvA introduces optimisation and machine learning together through cases about social problems.
Both develop Python programming and computational problem solving.
UvA devotes a course to visualising and communicating results. UCR includes visualisation in Introduction to Data Science.
Both prepare and explore data for analysis. UCR also practises data visualisation.
Both study data structures, efficient algorithms and computational problem solving.
Both cover regression, classification, feature engineering and model evaluation.
Both use models for text classification and generation. UvA also teaches retrieval, while UCR covers image and time-series applications.
Both cover databases. UvA places data management alongside enterprise systems and other digital technologies.

notes.text: UvA combines business, computing and mathematics in a dedicated sequence with two operations research courses, specialist projects and a 12 EC thesis made up of two courses. The UCR options offer related study with a different balance of methods and applications.

audience.programmeDescription: Business Analytics at UvA uses mathematics, statistics, computing and AI to study how organisations make decisions. Students apply these methods to business problems and carry out a supervised research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options explore a balance of business and analytics, a technical focus on algorithms and AI, or a business focus on markets and finance.
